primary_sources.title: The /proc Filesystem — Linux Kernel documentation
claims: /proc exposes process and system state including task states, /proc/stat and /proc/loadavg
procs_running counts threads running or ready to run

primary_sources.title: CPU load — Linux Kernel documentation
claims: Linux exports CPU time accounting through /proc/stat and /proc/uptime for userland monitoring tools
CPU percentage fields must be interpreted as sampled time in states rather than as load average

primary_sources.title: PSI - Pressure Stall Information — Linux Kernel documentation
claims: CPU, memory and I/O pressure are exposed through /proc/pressure
cgroup v2 can expose per-cgroup pressure files for scoped resource-pressure diagnosis

primary_sources.title: Control Group v2 — Linux Kernel documentation
claims: cgroup v2 exposes memory.current, memory.events and memory.pressure for scoped memory accounting and pressure/event diagnosis

primary_sources.title: iostat manual — sysstat upstream
claims: the first iostat report normally covers time since boot and subsequent reports cover time since the previous report; -y omits the first report
%util near 100% can indicate saturation for serial request-serving devices but does not reflect performance limits for parallel devices such as RAID arrays and modern SSDs

primary_sources.title: sar manual — sysstat upstream
claims: sar can collect, save and later report system activity records, enabling historical incident-window analysis

primary_sources.title: top manual — procps-ng upstream
claims: top is a procps-ng process/system activity view and should be treated as one sampled view among multiple sources rather than a root-cause oracle

primary_sources.title: strace project documentation
claims: strace traces system calls and signals and is intended for scoped process-level diagnosis
